Hello everyone.

I would like to ask you one question, I think a Yes or Not is enough, but long responses are wellcome too.  

I'm working in a Questionnaire with 34 questions, all of them in Likert Scale response (1-5) (NOT CONTINUOUS). I've adjusted a model with 5 factors. I used for it "Factor" a software developed by Lorenzo-Seva (2013) et al. focus in categorical variables.

The results have sense but I would like to do a CONFIRMATORY ANALYSIS. 

Is lavaan capable to do this kind of Analysis?

The model would be:


model <- '
   # latent variables
     labor =~ v1 + v3 + v5 + v6 + v8 + v10
     delivery =~ v2 + v4 + v7 + v9 + v11
     SupportBaby =~ v12 + v13 + v14 + v15 + v16
     midwiwes =~ v17 + v19 + v21 + v23 + v25 + v27 + v29 + v31 + v33
     doctors =~ v18 + v20 + v22 + v24 + v26 + v28 + v30 + v32 + v34
'
  
Thank you for your time.

On 07/08/2014 01:24 PM, Avinash CH wrote:
> data<-read.spss("Aguila_Screened_Var.sav",use.value.labels=FALSE,to.data.frame=TRUE)

Is this file in the current directory? You can get the current directory
by typing:

getwd()

and change it with setwd(); or you can give the full path to the file,
as in, say,

data<-read.spss("c:\temp\Aguila_Screened_Var.sav", ...)

Before you do anything else, make sure you have read in the data
properly. Compute some descriptives, and so on.

Yves.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Could I use lavaan to this aim?
parts: I'm trying to do a CFA with lavaan and I've some doubts. I have 34 categorical variables (Likert 5 options) but I don want to use dummy variables (it would be 136 binary variables). Could I use polychoric matrix? in that case, which estimator should I use?  DWLS?

No, you don't use dummy variables, just the 34 ordinal indicators.  When you give lavaan ordinal data, it will use the appropriate estimator by default (DWLS for point estimates, robust SEs) and will automatically estimate the thresholds and polychoric correlations before fitting the model to the polychoric correlation matrix.  You can either set the class of your variables to "ordered" in the data frame, or you can simply tell lavaan() or cfa() which variable names to treat as ordinal, as shown on the lavavan web site:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Terry
